open_points.subject: Cabinet's project context
open_points.text: “Consumer services — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet. … Each … validates a project id and reads its context in the disclosure class its token allows” conflicts with “`context` … answers only a trusted service whose token allows `personal_data` — today PresuPro and Client Portal.”
open_points.question: What Registry operation and concrete output lets Cabinet read project context, or is the promise that Cabinet reads context to be removed?
options: Give Cabinet a token allowing the existing `personal_data` context
Define a non-personal Cabinet projection
State that Cabinet validates ids but does not read context
open_points.default_guess: State that Cabinet validates project ids but does not read context.

open_points.subject: Legacy VPS migration source
open_points.text: “Test instances — any other instance … Each holds … no production personal data” conflicts with the import source being “the instances on the VPS and on the test rig” and the import carrying customers, objects and their personal data into production.
open_points.question: Is the legacy VPS Registry a test instance forbidden to hold production personal data, or a separately named migration source allowed to hold it until migration?
options: Name the VPS Registry as a legacy production migration source and exempt it from the test-instance rule
Classify it as a test instance and require its export to contain no production personal data
Remove the VPS as an import source
open_points.default_guess: Treat the VPS Registry as a separately named legacy production migration source until its one successful import.

open_points.subject: Agent projection personal values
open_points.text: The action promises “no display name … address, customer or other personal value,” while R0-68 says room names and artifact-pointer values are not inspected and “a value that breaks [the writer rule] is not refused and does reach the agent.”
open_points.question: Does Registry guarantee that the agent projection contains no personal value, or only that fields classified by Registry as `personal_data` are omitted even though unchecked free text may contain personal values?
options: Weaken the projection promise to exclude only declared `personal_data` fields
Validate or redact room names and pointer values before returning them
Remove unchecked room names and pointer values from the agent projection
open_points.default_guess: State that Registry excludes declared `personal_data` fields but cannot guarantee that unchecked writer-controlled values contain no personal information.

open_points.subject: Anonymised project artifact pointers
open_points.text: R0-62 says an anonymised project keeps artifact pointers, R0-68 says Registry does not inspect pointer values and a violating value may contain personal information, but R0-71 says the anonymised project “holds no personal value.”
open_points.question: What happens to artifact pointers whose `uri`, `payload_ref` or digest may identify a person when a project is anonymised?
options: Require the owner to remove or replace identifying pointers before anonymisation
Inspect and redact or reject identifying pointer values
Retain all pointers and withdraw the promise that an anonymised project holds no personal value
open_points.default_guess: Require confirmation that retained pointers are non-identifying, otherwise refuse anonymisation until they are withdrawn or replaced.

open_points.subject: Customer erasure and identifying links
open_points.text: R0-52 says “the personal data and the links that identify a person are removed,” while R0-06 and R0-67 say an erased Customer keeps its identity and “projects keep naming it.”
open_points.question: When customer contact data is erased, must projects stop carrying that `customer_ref`, or is the surviving Customer identity and project link explicitly exempt from removal of identifying links?
options: Keep `customer_ref` and declare it non-identifying after contact erasure
Remove the customer link from every project during customer erasure
Keep an internal link but suppress it from all outputs
open_points.default_guess: Keep the identity and project links as the later explicit decisions require, and narrow R0-52 so it does not claim those links are removed.

open_points.subject: Listing rooms of an anonymised project
open_points.text: R0-62 says an anonymised project keeps “its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else” and specifies the behavior of `validate`, artifact reads, project reads, `context`, the agent projection and project lists, but neither it nor “list rooms” says what listing its removed rooms returns.
open_points.question: What observable result does `list rooms` return for an anonymised project that still exists but no longer keeps rooms?
options: Refuse with the same erased result as `read a project`
Return an empty room list
Treat it as not found
Return an archived-project result with no rooms
open_points.default_guess: Refuse with the same erased result used by `read a project` and the agent projection.

open_points.subject: Audit coverage
open_points.text: The audit promise is defined through “significant changes of state” and the broad categories “changes to projects and customer records,” without saying whether room creation, artifact publication or withdrawal, session registration, pending requests, active-project changes, relationship ending or resuming, and failed confirmed actions are entries.
open_points.question: Exactly which primary actions create an audit entry, including whether refused attempts are logged?
options: Enumerate every audited primary action
Audit every successful state-changing primary action
Audit only the specifically named project, customer, grant, revoke, restriction and erasure actions
Audit confirmed failures as well as successful changes
open_points.default_guess: Audit every successful state-changing primary action and confirmed refused attempt, while excluding ordinary reads and flow-internal steps.

open_points.subject: Observable access-request outcome
open_points.text: “the session reads the outcome in its access” is not always true when access contains only granted ids, active project, pending status and version: granting a project already in the set and declining the request both clear the pending request without necessarily changing the set or active project.
open_points.question: How can the session distinguish a grant from a decline when granting produces no change to its existing granted set?
options: Refuse answering with ‘grant’ when the selected project is already granted
Store and expose the last request outcome
Return the outcome once through Kernel without storing it
Define such a no-op grant as indistinguishable from a decline and remove the promise
open_points.default_guess: Refuse a grant answer when the selected project is already granted, so the access-state transition remains observable.
